value.name: SGIP - Residential Solar and Storage Equity
value.administrator: Pacific Gas and Electric Company (PG&E), under the CPUC's Self-Generation Incentive Program
value.description: Storage incentive of $1,100/kWh paired with a solar incentive of $3,100/kW, funded via a $280 million CPUC-authorized statewide budget that opened for reservations June 2, 2025 and remains an active program per SGIP's own statewide announcements (most recently dated 2026-07-23). Administered across PG&E's entire distribution territory, which includes Oakdale/Stanislaus County.
value.eligibility: PG&E, SCE, or SDG&E residential customers (general market tier)

battery_programs.notes: Reused as a utility-level fact already established for other IOU-territory records this session: the CPUC-administered SGIP program applies uniformly across the named utility's entire distribution territory, directly verified via SGIP's own site (selfgenca.com) / the CPUC's own SGIP program page, including a program-status announcement as recent as 2026-07-23 confirming the program remains active.

value.name: Standard plan and checklist of all requirements, published on the City's website, substantially conforming to the California Solar Permitting Guidebook

required_documents.notes: Per Oakdale Municipal Code Section 7-84(a),(d)-(e): the Building Division adopts a standard plan and checklist substantially conforming to the CA Solar Permitting Guidebook, made available on the City's website.

value: Only one inspection is required for small residential rooftop solar energy systems eligible for expedited review, performed by the Building Division
The inspection is scheduled within two business days of a request
If the system fails inspection, a subsequent (re-)inspection is authorized
inspection_steps.notes: Per Oakdale Municipal Code Section 7-85(f)-(h), directly read via ecode360.com.

value.notes: Oakdale Municipal Code Section 7-85(a) states expedited applications shall receive a permit 'within three business days.' The City's own current 'Instant Residential Solar, Battery Storage and Electric Vehicle Charger Permits' page (Symbium platform) confirms an even faster instant-issuance pathway is now also available: 'your permit will be issued automatically, without manual review or an in-person visit.' The general (non-expedited) 'two to four weeks' figure quoted on the Building Division page applies to ordinary building permits, not this solar-specific expedited/instant pathway, and is not used here.

value.program_or_pathway: Small Residential Rooftop Solar Energy System Permitting (municipal code Article XII); current applications are processed via the Symbium instant online permitting platform
other_conditions: Systems must be installed on single- or duplex-family dwellings
Solar panel arrays cannot exceed the maximum legal building height as defined by the city
Routine operation and maintenance or like-kind replacements do not require a permit
Symbium automatically verifies State/local code compliance as well as contractor and business license status

eligibility_constraints.notes: Upgraded this session with directly-confirmed size caps (10kW AC / 30kW thermal) from Municipal Code Section 7-81's definition of 'Small residential rooftop solar energy system.'
